title: Localization and multiplication of the Proj graded comparison
statement:
Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $T$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and $\psi:A\to\Gamma_*(T,L)$ a graded ring homomorphism [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. Set $U=\bigcup_{e>0,\ f\in A_e}T_{\psi(f)}$, using the nonvanishing opens [def-sc-section-generating-locus], and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj]. Let $r:U\to P$ be the canonical morphism, specified by $r^{-1}D_+(f)=T_{\psi(f)}$ and by the degree-zero chart formula $r^\sharp(b/f^q)=\psi(b)/\psi(f)^q$ for $b\in A_{qe}$, $q\geq0$. There is a unique family of $\mathcal O_U$-linear maps $\theta_m:r^*\mathcal O_P(m)\to L^{\otimes m}|_U$, $m\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with the following chart normalization: for every $e>0$, $f\in A_e$, $q\geq0$, and $b\in A_{m+qe}$, the pullback of the fraction $b/f^q$ on $D_+(f)$ is sent on $T_{\psi(f)}$ to $\psi(b)/\psi(f)^q$. Division means the inverse of multiplication by the free generator $\psi(f)^q$ of $L^{\otimes qe}$ on this open. These chart maps commute with restriction and agree on overlaps. Each global homogeneous section $b\in A_m$ is sent to $\psi(b)|_U$. The family respects the unit and the graded multiplication maps: for all $m,n\geq0$,
$$\theta_{m+n}\circ r^*(\mu^P_{m,n})=\mu^L_{m,n}\circ(\theta_m\otimes\theta_n),$$
where the canonical tensor-pullback comparison identifies the sources, $\mu^P$ is induced by multiplication of homogeneous fractions and $\mu^L$ is tensor multiplication of powers of $L$. No degree-generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), proof: extension to the localized graded algebra; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), local bases and gluing.

proof.text: Fix $m\geq0$, $f\in A_e$, $e>0$, and put $W_f=T_{\psi(f)}$, $s=\psi(f)|_{W_f}$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], the sections of $\mathcal O_P(m)$ on $D_+(f)$ are precisely the homogeneous fractions $b/f^q$ with $b\in A_{m+qe}$. By [def-sc-section-generating-locus], multiplication by $s$ is an isomorphism $L^{\otimes m}|_{W_f}\to L^{\otimes(m+e)}|_{W_f}$: locally in a frame of $L$, it is multiplication by the unit representing $s$. Define $\alpha_{m,f}(b/f^q)=\psi(b)|_{W_f}/s^q$. If $b/f^q=b'/f^{q'}$, then $f^k(f^{q'}b-f^qb')=0$ for some $k\geq0$. Applying the graded map $\psi$ and cancelling the invertible multiplication maps $s^k$ and $s^{q+q'}$ gives $\psi(b)/s^q=\psi(b')/s^{q'}$. Thus the formula is independent of representatives, including when $f$ is a zero divisor.

source.place: Tag 01NK (lemma-invertible-map-into-proj), localized extension; Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), division by a generating section

proof.text:
These maps are additive and semilinear for the given $r^\sharp$. Explicitly, common denominators give
$$\alpha_{m,f}(b/f^q+b'/f^{q'})=(\psi(b)s^{q'}+\psi(b')s^q)/s^{q+q'}=\alpha_{m,f}(b/f^q)+\alpha_{m,f}(b'/f^{q'}).$$
For $a\in A_{te}$, the specified scalar chart map and the tensor multiplication in [def-sc-invertible-section-ring] give
$$\alpha_{m,f}((a/f^t)(b/f^q))=\psi(ab)/s^{t+q}=r^\sharp(a/f^t)\,\alpha_{m,f}(b/f^q).$$
Zero is sent to zero. Thus $\alpha_{m,f}$ is an $A_{(f)}$-linear map into $\Gamma(W_f,L^{\otimes m})$, whose scalar action is through $r^\sharp$.

source.place: Tag 01NK, existence: the localized extension is a graded ring map

proof.text:
For an inclusion $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ with $g$ homogeneous of positive degree, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] (a) to $A(m)$: there are $k\geq1$ and homogeneous $a$ with $g^k=af$, and restriction sends $b/f^q$ to $a^qb/g^{kq}$. The preimage equality for $r$ gives $W_g\subseteq W_f$. On $W_g$, both $\psi(g)$ and $\psi(f)$ freely generate their respective powers of $L$, and $\psi(g)^k=\psi(a)\psi(f)$. Consequently
$$\frac{\psi(a)^q\psi(b)}{\psi(g)^{kq}}=\frac{\psi(b)}{\psi(f)^q}.$$
This is obtained by multiplying by the invertible denominator $\psi(g)^{kq}\psi(f)^q$ and using the displayed relation; it requires no cancellation in $A$. Hence the $\alpha_{m,f}$ commute with every restriction between standard opens. In particular the two maps restrict equally on the common chart $D_+(fg)=D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)$.

source.place: Tags 01M4 (lemma-standard-open) and 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), restrictions for A(m); Tag 01NK, uniqueness on localizations

proof.text: The standard opens form a basis of $P$: the complement of $V_+(I)$ is the union of $D_+(h)$ over homogeneous $h\in I$; their finite intersections are $D_+(fg)$. Put $F_m=\mathcal O_P(m)$ and $G_m=r_*(L^{\otimes m}|_U)$, a sheaf of $\mathcal O_P$-modules with $G_m(V)=\Gamma(r^{-1}V,L^{\otimes m})$ and scalars through $r^\sharp$, as in [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. The preceding steps give compatible maps on this basis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] to the underlying abelian sheaves to obtain $\alpha_m:F_m\to G_m$. Its components are $\mathcal O_P$-linear: for any open $V$ and sections $a,u$ on $V$, the equality $\alpha_m(au)=r^\sharp(a)\alpha_m(u)$ holds after restriction to each basis open inside $V$, hence holds by the sheaf condition. The adjunction in [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $\theta_m:r^*F_m\to L^{\otimes m}|_U$. In the tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback], its local rule is $t\otimes u\mapsto t\alpha_m(u)$, so on pulled-back fractions it has exactly the required normalization. This gives a single global map in each degree, hence the asserted agreement on overlaps.

source.place: Tag 009U (lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules), and Tag 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); Constructions Tag 01NK, local construction and gluing

proof.text:
For $b\in A_m$, [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] identifies its restriction on each $D_+(f)$ with $b/1$. Taking $q=0$ therefore sends its pullback to $\psi(b)|_{W_f}$, hence to $\psi(b)|_U$ since the $W_f$ cover $U$. In degree zero $\alpha_{0,f}(a/f^q)=r^\sharp(a/f^q)$; in particular $1\mapsto1$, so $\theta_0$ is the unit map. For $b\in A_{m+qe}$ and $c\in A_{n+te}$, the multiplication maps in the statement satisfy
$$\alpha_{m+n,f}(bc/f^{q+t})=\frac{\psi(bc)}{s^{q+t}}=\frac{\psi(b)}{s^q}\frac{\psi(c)}{s^t}.$$
Here the last product is the tensor multiplication of [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. Locally, the tensor-pullback identification sends $(u\otimes x)\otimes(v\otimes y)$ to $uv\otimes(x\otimes y)$ by the balanced tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-module-pullback]. A germ of each pulled-back factor is a sum of scalar multiples of pulled-back fraction germs, since $r(x)$ lies in the standard-open basis. Bilinearity extends the displayed equality to these sums. Equality of the two sheaf maps follows locally on sections, proving the required multiplication identity for every $m,n$, including zero.

source.place: Tag 01NK, property (2) and the graded-algebra comparison; Tag 01N8, fraction formula and tensor multiplication

proof.text: If $\theta'_m$ is another family with the stated chart normalization, transpose it by [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] to $\alpha'_m:\mathcal O_P(m)\to r_*(L^{\otimes m}|_U)$. The tensor adjunction rule sends $u$ to $\theta'_m(1\otimes u)$. Thus $\alpha'_m$ and $\alpha_m$ agree on every fraction on every standard open; these are all sections there by [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. They are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis], and the adjunction bijection implies $\theta'_m=\theta_m$ for every $m$. This also covers $U=\varnothing$, when all target section modules are zero. No step assumed that $A$ was generated in degree one, that any twist was invertible on all of $P$, or that $T$ was quasi-compact.

lean.note: The normalized family is unique among all families satisfying the fraction normalization. Division is expressed equivalently after multiplication by the free denominator. The unit and graded multiplication equalities are expressed on actual pulled-back sections on every open; these locally generate the tensor pullback, so this is the full sheaf-map compatibility under the canonical tensor-pullback comparison.
